# Round-12 filed predictions (generated by `predict_r12.py`; hashed pre-request)

Generated from COMMITTED prior-round bytes only — r8
`corpus/evidence/round8-horizon/results.jsonl`) and r11
`corpus/evidence/round11-power/results-r11.jsonl`). No round-12 request had
been made when this file was written; `ordering.log` pins the ordering. Rules
and every judgement literal live in `predict_r12.py` (also hashed).

## Event sets scored at close (design critic D6: reported separately, never
## pooled into one 'forecast skill' number without these splits)

| set | N | what it tests |
|---|---:|---|
| pass events | 416 | 5 family-1 arms x 64 problems + 2 family-2 arms x 48 |
| per-problem sign events | 304 | E3a/E3b/E3c/E4 x 64 + E5 x 48 |
| run-level events | 7 | RL1-RL7 below |
| **total scored events** | **727** | |

Brier = mean (p - outcome)^2 per set. BSS = 1 - Brier/Brier_climatology, where
the climatological forecast is each event's own group base rate: per-arm
observed pass rate for pass events, per-contrast observed win rate for sign
events, per-event observed rate for run-level events. **The pooled pass-event
BSS is labelled `persistence + arm-rate transport`, not generic forecast
skill**: family-1 predictions reuse r11 outcomes on the SAME problems, and
family-2 predictions are constant per arm by design. Reported splits: (i)
family-1 replicate arms (`A-CKPT4710`, `A-CKPT710` — the arms with r11
per-problem evidence), (ii) family-1 novel arms (`A-INC`, `A-CKPT10`,
`A-MONO` — base rate + transported difficulty slope only), (iii) family 2
(constant per arm). Excluded pids (error records) are dropped from BOTH the
score and its climatology, never scored as failures.

Calibration: slope + intercept from a logistic recalibration of outcome on
logit(p), probabilities clipped to [1e-06, 1-1e-06] before the
logit (critic D5), damped Newton, <=50 iterations, tol 1e-10; reported for the
416 pass events (primary) and for all 727 events
(secondary). Reliability: 5 equal-width bins on p; an empty bin prints
`pred=n/a obs=n/a n=0` (critic D8).

## 1. Arm base rates and their derivation rule

| arm | base rate | rule |
|---|---:|---|
| `A-INC` | 0.6429 | r8 7/10 shrunk with k=4 toward 0.5 |
| `A-CKPT4710` | 0.4531 | r11 29/64 raw (n>=20) |
| `A-CKPT710` | 0.3281 | r11 21/64 raw (n>=20) |
| `A-CKPT10` | 0.2031 | linear extrapolation in checkpoint count from the r11 pair (3 ckpts 0.4531, 2 ckpts 0.3281 -> 1 ckpt) |
| `A-MONO` | 0.1429 | r8 0/10 shrunk with k=4 toward 0.5 |
| `T-DENSE` | 0.4531 | family-1 dense arm rate (transport-of-base-rate null) |
| `T-SPARSE` | 0.3281 | family-1 sparse arm rate (transport-of-base-rate null) |

Shrinkage rule: raw rate when the prior evidence has n>=20; otherwise
(successes + 4*0.5)/(n + 4). `A-CKPT10` has no direct
observation, so it is linearly extrapolated in checkpoint count from the r11
pair. Family-2 arms inherit the family-1 dense/sparse rates as an explicit
transport-of-base-rate null.

## 2. Difficulty tilt (fitted on r11's committed per-problem bytes)

Logistic fit on 128 r11 (pid,arm) final-pass outcomes, features
[1, I(arm=A-CKPT710), x_pid - xbar] where x_pid = mean of that pid's r11
mean `nwrong` at {7,10} over both arms, xbar = 0.886719:

    intercept a = -0.967857
    arm(710) b  = -1.224164
    difficulty c = -5.025712   (per unit of x_pid - xbar)

r12 per-problem probability:

    p = clip( sigmoid( logit(base_arm) + c*(x_pid - xbar) + delta_arm ) )

clipped to [0.02, 0.98]. `delta_arm` is a mean-preserving offset
solved by bisection per arm so that the arm's mean predicted probability
equals its §1 base rate exactly (the fitted slope is steep; without the
offset the sigmoid saturates and the arm marginal drifts — measured before
the fix: A-MONO mean p 0.372 against a 0.143 base rate). Consequence: each
arm's predicted pass count equals base_arm x n by construction, and the tilt
only redistributes probability ACROSS problems.

| arm | delta_arm | mean p | min p | max p |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `A-INC` | +0.3951 | 0.6429 | 0.0200 | 0.9800 |
| `A-CKPT4710` | -0.8111 | 0.4531 | 0.0200 | 0.9694 |
| `A-CKPT710` | -1.5190 | 0.3281 | 0.0200 | 0.9021 |
| `A-CKPT10` | -2.2325 | 0.2031 | 0.0200 | 0.7020 |
| `A-MONO` | -2.5711 | 0.1429 | 0.0200 | 0.5234 |
| `T-DENSE` | +0.0000 | 0.4531 | 0.4531 | 0.4531 |
| `T-SPARSE` | +0.0000 | 0.3281 | 0.3281 | 0.3281 |

The fitted arm intercepts are NOT reused for arms other than the two r11
arms; those take the §1 base rates. Family-2 problems have no prior x_pid,
so they get the constant base rate (no tilt, delta = 0).

**Persistence-skill caveat (design critic D6).** `x_pid` is the mean of that
pid's r11 mean `nwrong` at {7,10} over both arms, so it includes r11's
turn-10 value — the same turn whose r12 pass is the prediction target. This
is not within-run circularity (different run, different day, a fresh context
per ladder, no cross-run state on the served unit), but the fitted slope is
therefore a *persistence-of-difficulty* coefficient and C5's skill claim may
only be read as persistence skill against arm climatology, never as cold
forecasting.

| quantity | predicted | derivation |
|---|---:|---|
| E3a 4710-INC at {4,7,10} | +0.6667 | r8 paired per-pid mean at {4,7,10}, n=10 (committed bytes) |
| E2/E3b 710-4710 at {7,10} | +0.3520 | r11 paired per-pid mean, n=64 (recomputed +0.3516, published +0.352) |
| E3c 10-710 at {10} | +0.3281 | one-step linear extrapolation in removed checkpoints using r11's final-turn step (+0.3281) |
| E4 MONO-CKPT10 final | +0.0437 | r8 paired MONO-CKPT4710 final gap (+0.7000) minus two extrapolated final-turn steps (2 x +0.3281) |
| E5 SPARSE-DENSE at {7,10} (family 2) | +0.1758 | r11 dose x ATTENUATE=0.5 (stated prior, not a measurement) |

Committed inputs: r11 paired dose {7,10} +0.3516 (sd 0.8198, n=64, dz=0.4288); r11 per-problem wins 26/64; r8 paired gap {4,7,10} +0.6667 (n=10); r8 paired MONO-CKPT4710 final +0.7000; r11 final-turn step +0.3281; r8 final-turn step +1.1000.

## 5. Run-level probabilistic predictions (judgement, frozen by the hash)

| id | event | P | justification |
|---|---|---:|---|
| RL1 | E1 Page p < 0.05 AND direction increasing (LADDER ESTABLISHED) | 0.55 | power_analysis_r12.md gives >=0.98 power at the anchored alternative, but the anchor's INC leg comes from r8 at n=10 in a different batch; the binding risk is anchor validity, not power, so 0.55 not 0.9 |
| RL2 | E2 verdict = REPEATS-r11 (diff>0, p<0.05, sign agrees) | 0.70 | r11 fired the same rule at p=0.0011 on these exact problems; batch variability (r8 1/10, r9 2/8+2/8, r11 29/64+21/64) is the residual risk |
| RL3 | E2 additionally POINT-MATCHES-r11 (|diff - 0.352| <= 0.15) | 0.45 | the r11 point estimate has a 95% CI half-width of 0.205, wider than the 0.15 window |
| RL4 | all three adjacent diffs (E3) > 0 | 0.50 | the INC leg is the only one never measured at n>=44; sign agreement across three gaps is a conjunction |
| RL5 | E4 verdict = DISSOCIATION ESTABLISHED | 0.20 | the mechanical point prediction below is +0.044, i.e. essentially null: r8's MONO-CKPT4710 gap (+0.700) is almost exactly consumed by two extrapolated final-turn steps (2 x +0.328) |
| RL6 | E5 verdict = TRANSPORTS (family-2 dose diff>0, p<0.05) | 0.45 | attenuation prior 0.5 x dz=0.4288 -> dz=0.214, at which n=48 has 0.327 power (power_r12.py §4); unattenuated it has 0.842 |
| RL7 | E6 verdict = FORECAST SKILLED (BSS>0 AND slope in [0.5,2.0]) | 0.50 | the persistence predictor should beat arm climatology on family-1 replicate arms but is constant-per-arm on family 2, where BSS is ~0 by construction |

Brier over these seven events is reported separately (r11's 3-event Brier of
0.153 is the comparator; 7 events is still small and is labelled as such).

## 6. Preregistered verdict rule

Applied verbatim from `probe_plan_r12.md` §2.3 (R1-R5), including the neutral-
sign downgrade (wins == losses counts as DISAGREEMENT), the degenerate-input
conventions (sd=0 -> t=0.000, p=1.0000; var_L=0 -> z=0.000, p=1.0000), and the
`UNDERPOWERED-INDETERMINATE` override when a family's analysed n falls below
the filed power floor (`power_analysis_r12.md`).
